To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the antiviral maintenance treatment (AMT) is effective in the treatment of recurrent HCV after liver transplantation.

(1) AMT with pegylated interferon and ribavrin is effective in preventing graft reinfection and fibrosis progression in liver transplant recipients, (2) AMT with interferon alfa-2b and ribavrin has limited efficacy and is poorly tolerated in liver transplant recipients.
the antiviral maintenance treatment is effective in the majority of liver recipients with recurrent hepatitis.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (i) the role of the immune system in the pathogenesis of HCV infection and its role in the response to antiviral therapy (AT); (ii) the molecular mechanisms underlying HCV resistance and the development of resistance to AT in HCV‐infected patients; (iii) the molecular basis of HCV pathogenicity and its role in liver damage; (iv) the molecular mechanisms of the interaction between HCV and the immune system and the development of new
a study of the role of the social environment in the development of social behavior and social competence.
the development of novel methods for the analysis of the structure and properties of complex systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence is inadequate to recommend or not recommend the use of interferon-α2b and/or ribavirin for the treatment of chronic hepatitis C infection in liver transplant recipients.
the use of antiviral therapy with interferon and Ribavirin is effective and safe for the treatment of recurrent hepatitis C in liver transplant recipients.
the evidence for the use of antiviral maintenance treatment (AMT) in liver transplant recipients (LTRs) with recurrent hepatitis C (HCV) is limited and inconclusive.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of interferon‐α and ribavirin maintenance therapy for recurrent hepatitis C in liver transplant recipients was associated with a significant reduction in liver fibrosis.
the combination of ribavirin and interferon‐α is an effective antiviral treatment for patients with recurrent hepatitis C after transplantation.

interferon/ribavirin therapy is safe and feasible in liver transplant patients with recurrent hepatitis C, but it is unlikely that it will be able to eradicate hepatitis C in a large percentage of these patients.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a 48-week course of pegylated interferon and ribavarin in the maintenance setting for patients who had previously failed a course of therapy was not effective.
we have developed a method for using a combination of two different types of interferons, alpha-2a and alpha-2b, to treat patients with HCV.
